title: Theory of constraints: stop starting new businesses, remove the one thing blocking growth
summary: Alex uses three founder conversations to argue that plateaued businesses are stuck on a skill gap, not market saturation. The fix is to name the single constraint, phrase it as a "how do I" question, and put all effort there instead of launching another business.

principles.text: The only excusable reason to plateau is exhausting your total addressable market; otherwise you just don't know how.
principles.quote: the only reason a business should plateau that is reasonable, that is not your fault, is that you have reached the total addressable market.

principles.text: A system grows until it hits a constraint; remove it and growth continues until the next constraint.
principles.quote: a system will grow until it is constrained, right? It has a constraint, and then once you remove the constraint, it'll continue to grow. until it reaches another constraint.

principles.text: Prioritize problems: usually only one or two things truly constrain growth, and only one is the real constraint at a time.
principles.quote: one of the things that we have done well is prioritizing what problems to solve.

principles.text: Ask a specific question like 'what's stopping us from $5M a month?' rather than 'why am I not growing?'
principles.quote: what's stopping us from being at $5 million a month? What's stopping us? And until we can clearly answer that question, there's nothing else we need to do.

principles.text: Reframe skill deficiencies as 'how do I...' questions so they become solvable problems.
principles.quote: let's phrase the deficiency as a question, which is how do I learn how to recruit, manage, and train a sales team.

principles.text: A new business won't fix a stall because you carry your own ceiling into it; businesses grow to the entrepreneur's level of incompetence.
principles.quote: the businesses will grow to the level of incompetence of the entrepreneur. So if you're a $4 million entrepreneur, the next business will be a $4 million business.
